# Tenset

> Free, no-account web app for planning a weekly gym program. It shows weekly sets per muscle group on a body map. Programs live only in the user's browser; a share link (`/shared#...`) carries the whole program, and opening it shows a preview with a Save button.

AI agents can build a program for the user and hand back that link. Nothing is stored on the server; send programs with POST so they stay out of request logs.

## Option 1: MCP server (preferred)

- URL: `https://tenset-app.vercel.app/api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless, no auth)
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http tenset https://tenset-app.vercel.app/api/mcp`
- claude.ai: Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector, paste the URL.
- Tools: `get_reference`, `search_exercises`, `list_splits`, `create_program`, `read_program`

## Option 2: plain HTTP (no MCP client needed)

Same tools, JSON responses, CORS open. Base: `https://tenset-app.vercel.app/api/agent/`

- `GET /api/agent/reference`: muscle group, equipment, pattern and day ids, plus input limits
- `GET /api/agent/splits`: ready-made split templates with ranked exercise options per slot
- `GET /api/agent/exercises?query=&group=&pattern=&equipment=&limit=`: search the catalog. `equipment` is a comma-separated list of what the user has (`equipment=` empty means bodyweight only)
- `POST /api/agent/program` with the JSON body: validates the program and returns `url` (the share link) plus weekly sets per muscle group
- `POST /api/agent/read` with `{"link": "..."}`: turns a share link back into the program JSON so it can be edited

Send programs and links with POST. Only if your tool cannot POST, use `GET /api/agent/program?program=<url-encoded JSON>` or `GET /api/agent/read?link=<url-encoded share link>`: a GET puts the user's program in the request address, which hosting logs may keep for a short time.

Errors come back as HTTP 400 with `{"error", "problems": [...]}` describing what to fix. Limits: 40 exercises per day, search queries up to 200 characters, request bodies up to 128 KB (larger bodies get HTTP 413).

## Workflow

1. Ask the user how many days they train, what equipment they have, and any focus.
2. Get ids from `reference`, then pick exercises with `exercises` (filter by the user's equipment) or start from a template in `splits`.
3. Send the program to `program` and give the user the returned `url`.
4. Check `weeklySets`: `band: "target"` means the sets fall in the intended range for most groups, and `target: [low, high]` gives that range in weekly sets. Read any `notes` (adjustments that did not block the program). Keep wording neutral.

## Program JSON

```json
{
  "name": "Full body",
  "days": [
    { "day": 0, "label": "A", "entries": [
      { "exerciseId": 401, "sets": 3, "reps": "6-10", "restSec": 180, "rir": 2 },
      { "exerciseId": 101, "sets": 3, "restSec": 90 },
      { "exerciseId": 304, "sets": 3, "supersetWithPrevious": true }
    ] },
    { "day": 3, "entries": [{ "exerciseId": 501, "sets": 3 }] }
  ]
}
```

- `day`: 0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday. Days left out are rest days.
- `exerciseId`: a catalog id from `exercises`, or a custom id `"c1"`..`"c63"` defined in an optional `custom` array. Custom exercises take `id`, `name`, `equipment` (ids), `laterality` (`bilateral`, `unilateral` or `alternating`) and `groups` (`{ "<group id>": "primary" | "secondary" }`).
- `reps` is optional (defaults to the exercise's own range). `sets` 1 to 20. `name` up to 40 characters.
- `restSec` is optional: rest between sets in whole seconds, 0 to 600, rounded to the nearest 15.
- `rir` is optional: target reps in reserve, a whole number 0 to 5.
- `supersetWithPrevious: true` pairs the entry with the one above it. Supersets are pairs only: on the first entry of a day, or on an entry whose predecessor is already paired, it is ignored and the response lists it in `notes`.
- The summary marks pairs as `(superset A1)` and `(superset A2)`, and lists rest and RIR after sets and reps, e.g. `Barbell Bench Press: 3 x 6-8, rest 180s, RIR 2`.

Example (Monday squat, bench, row; Thursday Romanian deadlift):

```sh
curl -X POST https://tenset-app.vercel.app/api/agent/program \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Full body","days":[{"day":0,"entries":[{"exerciseId":401,"sets":3},{"exerciseId":101,"sets":3},{"exerciseId":304,"sets":3}]},{"day":3,"entries":[{"exerciseId":501,"sets":3}]}]}'
```
